sources.name: Kenney (kenney.nl), CC0 1.0
sources.terms: Five audio packs by Kenney: Sci-fi Sounds, Impact Sounds, Interface Sounds, UI Audio and Digital Audio. Each pack page lists the licence as "Creative Commons CC0" and each archive contains a License.txt that names CC0 1.0 (http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) and allows use in personal and commercial projects (three of the five also name educational projects). Credit is welcome but not required; it is given here anyway. The pack pages carry a robots meta tag with "noai" and a "tdm-reservation" marker. The files are used here as ordinary game sound material and for listening tests, not as training data for any model; if that ever changes, ask Kenney first. The .url shortcut files in the archives are not unpacked.

sources.name: NASA, public domain in general
sources.terms: Recordings hosted on nasa.gov and its subdomains (www.nasa.gov, images-assets.nasa.gov). NASA's Images and Media Usage Guidelines (https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/), read again on 2026-11-14, say that NASA content, audio included, "generally" is not subject to copyright in the United States and that NASA should be acknowledged as the source. The page then separates two kinds of use. NON-COMMERCIAL use (educational or informational; news outlets, schools, textbook authors) may go ahead without explicit permission when the content is used factually and without implying endorsement. COMMERCIAL use is described more narrowly: clearances may be necessary for material with NASA logos or NASA employees in cover art or promotional content; otherwise NASA material can generally be used editorially in published works that are not promotional in nature; commercial use, advertisements included, must not convey NASA's endorsement of goods or services; a recording with an identifiable person may infringe that person's privacy or publicity rights, so permission should be obtained; and currently employed astronauts and employees cannot have their names, likenesses or other personality traits shown on commercial products, advertisements or promotional material. Two more sections: NASA does not want its material used for NFTs or cryptocurrency, and a section on "super intelligence" (SI) applications says that NASA content used with such models must not be attributed to NASA and that the NASA insignia must not appear with their output; these recordings are used for neither. So the guidelines are not a blanket permission for a commercial game. This is the owner's decision to make, and nothing here is legal advice. What it means for this game: (1) nothing may suggest that NASA endorses the game or any product, and a store page or trailer is promotional, so NASA material and the NASA name need clearance there; (2) the NASA insignia, logos and emblems are not part of these files and must not be used without clearance; (3) every file with an identifiable voice, an astronaut or a flight controller, is marked "speech" or "probable" in downloads.json and in the Notes column below (the marks come from titles and pages, nobody has listened to all of them); these files are test material for the radio filter and for listening, and are not to be shipped without a separate decision, and the two ISS files, with a named astronaut who is currently employed by NASA, must never ship; (4) third-party material that NASA shows on its pages keeps its own rights; nothing of that kind was taken. Where a NASA page names someone besides NASA in the credit, the credit is recorded exactly: "NASA/University of Iowa" for the plasma wave recordings (the page states no restriction beyond NASA's guidelines), "NASA. Courtesy of the Electric and Magnetic Field Instrument Suite and Integrated Science (EMFISIS) team at the University of Iowa" for the chorus recording, "NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI/Univ of Iowa" for Juno, and the long Mars credits for Perseverance SuperCam. Pages read: https://www.nasa.gov/historical-sounds/, https://www.nasa.gov/sounds-from-beyond/, https://www.nasa.gov/artemisaudio/ ("All audio files are free to download and cleared for use in accordance with NASA's media usage guidelines."), https://www.nasa.gov/history/apollo-11-audio-highlights/, https://www.nasa.gov/missions/mms/nasa-listens-in-as-electrons-whistle-while-they-work/ and the NASA Image and Video Library.
